config.help: Your full Freshdesk host, as it appears in the address bar — `acme.freshdesk.com`, including the `.freshdesk.com` part
config.label: Freshdesk domain
config.name: domain

description: Freshdesk ticketing: list, read, create and update tickets and the contacts they belong to

contract.description: Verify credentials with a bounded contact read

operations.description: Verify credentials with a bounded contact read

params.description: Records to fetch; one is enough to prove the credential works
params.name: per_page

response_schema.description: The contacts, as a bare JSON array. With `per_page = 1` it holds one element; an empty array is still a successful credential check, because an account may genuinely have no contacts

params.description: Only tickets updated at or after this date
params.name: updated

response_schema.description: The matching tickets, as a bare JSON array with no envelope. The ticket bodies (`description`, `description_text`) are NOT included in a listing — read one ticket with `freshdesk-ticket-get` to get its text

fr_due_by.description: When a first response is due

fr_escalated.description: True when the first-response SLA was breached

responder_id.description: The agent it is assigned to; null when unassigned

source.description: How the ticket arrived: 1 Email, 2 Portal, 3 Phone, 7 Chat, 9 Feedback widget, 10 Outbound email

type.description: The ticket type, e.g. `Question` or `Incident`. Null when unset

custom_fields.description: The account's own ticket fields, keyed by field name — an object, unlike zendesk's array of `{id, value}` pairs

description_text.description: The same message as plain text. This is the one to summarize or quote

responder_id.description: The assigned agent; null when unassigned

source.description: 1 Email, 2 Portal, 3 Phone, 7 Chat, 9 Feedback widget, 10 Outbound email

structured_description.description: The message again, as `{description_contents: [{type, data: {content}}]}` — Freshdesk's block form

type.description: The ticket type, e.g. `Question` or `Incident`. Null when unset

contract.description: Create a ticket. The requester must be identified either by requester_id, or by phone together with name — Freshdesk states this only in prose and its required flags do not capture it

operations.description: Create a ticket. The requester must be identified either by requester_id, or by phone together with name — Freshdesk states this only in prose and its required flags do not capture it

params.description: Requester phone number. Supply with name, or supply requester_id instead
params.name: phone

params.description: Requester name. Supply with phone, or supply requester_id instead
params.name: name

params.description: Requester id. Supply this, or supply phone together with name
params.name: requester_id

params.description: Ticket description; HTML or long text
params.name: description

params.description: Ticket status: 2 open, 3 pending, 4 resolved, 5 closed
params.name: status

params.description: Ticket priority: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high, 4 urgent
params.name: priority

params.description: Channel the ticket came in on
params.name: source

params.description: Email config used for this ticket
params.name: email_config_id

params.description: Group the ticket is assigned to
params.name: group_id

params.description: Addresses to copy on the ticket
params.name: cc_emails

description_text.description: The opening message as plain text

id.description: The new ticket's id — the only place it is returned, and what every later call addresses

priority.description: 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 Urgent. Defaults to 1

requester_id.description: Set even when the ticket was created by phone and name — Freshdesk resolves or creates the contact and reports which one it used

source.description: 1 Email, 2 Portal, 3 Phone, 7 Chat, 9 Feedback widget, 10 Outbound email

status.description: 2 Open, 3 Pending, 4 Resolved, 5 Closed. Defaults to 2 when the create did not set it

params.description: Id of the ticket to update
params.name: id

params.description: Ticket status: 2 open, 3 pending, 4 resolved, 5 closed
params.name: status

params.description: Ticket priority: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high, 4 urgent
params.name: priority

params.description: Email config used for this ticket
params.name: email_config_id

params.description: Group the ticket is assigned to
params.name: group_id

description.description: The opening message as HTML — unchanged by an update, which never edits the first message

description_text.description: The opening message as plain text

status.description: 2 Open, 3 Pending, 4 Resolved, 5 Closed — the value **after** this update

tags.description: The ticket's tag set after the update. Freshdesk documents no additive form of this field — unlike zendesk's `additional_tags` — so read it back rather than assuming earlier tags survived

updated_at.description: Moves on every accepted update, so it is the cheapest confirmation that the call changed something

contract.description: Add a note to a ticket; the note is private unless explicitly made public

operations.description: Add a note to a ticket; the note is private unless explicitly made public

params.description: Whether the note is hidden from end users
params.name: private

params.description: Set true when the note originates from an external system
params.name: incoming

params.description: Addresses to notify about the note
params.name: notify_emails

id.description: The note's own id, distinct from the ticket's

incoming.description: True when the note represents something the customer sent in rather than an agent's own note

notified_to.description: Who was notified — the response's name for the request's `notify_emails`

private.description: True for a note only agents can see. Defaults to true — read it back before assuming a note was published

support_email.description: The support address involved, or null

ticket_id.description: The ticket the note was added to

user_id.description: Who the note is attributed to

contract.description: List and filter contacts, e.g. to resolve a caller before filing a ticket

operations.description: List and filter contacts, e.g. to resolve a caller before filing a ticket

response_schema.description: The matching contacts, as a bare JSON array with no envelope. Empty when nothing matched — which is a successful call, and the signal that the caller is not a known contact

email.description: The primary address; further ones are in `other_emails`

id.description: The contact id — this is the `requester_id` a ticket create takes

other_companies.description: Freshdesk's own examples disagree about this member: bare company ids in a listing, `{company_id, view_all_tickets}` objects on a single read. No item schema is declared rather than guessing which

avatar.description: The contact's picture — `{avatar_url, content_type, id, name, size}` — or null

custom_fields.description: The account's own contact fields, keyed by field name

devices.description: Known devices, each `{device_type, device_make, device_model, app_version, os, os_version}`

other_companies.description: On a single read Freshdesk's example shows `{company_id, view_all_tickets}` objects; its listing example shows bare ids. No item schema is declared rather than picking one

view_all_tickets.description: True when this contact can see every ticket of their company, not only their own

active.description: Whether the contact has an active portal account. Freshdesk's own create example returns `false`, so do not treat a create as producing an active contact

avatar.description: Null on a contact created through the API

id.description: The new contact's id — the `requester_id` for a following `freshdesk-ticket-create`
